questions.q: Which Hungarian obstetrician championed handwashing in the 1840s and died in an asylum?
questions.e: Proven right after his death. Wash your hands.

questions.q: Which bone is the only one in the body that doesn’t articulate with another bone?
questions.e: Held in place by muscles and ligaments alone.

questions.q: William Withering described which heart drug in 1785, from the foxglove plant?
‘Saturday night palsy’ is a compression injury of which nerve?
questions.e: Arm draped over a chair after a big night. Wrist drop follows.

questions.q: Which fungus causes ‘rose gardener’s disease’?
In the early seasons of ‘Grey’s Anatomy’, what was the hospital called?
questions.e: Later Seattle Grace Mercy West, then Grey Sloan Memorial.

questions.q: The word ‘malaria’ comes from Italian for what?
questions.e: Mala aria. Blame the swamps, not the mosquitoes.

questions.q: How long does a red blood cell live, on average?
Which US president secretly had Addison’s disease?
What is the photic sneeze reflex better known as, by its acronym?
questions.e: Sneezing on stepping into bright light. Autosomal dominant. Bless you.

questions.q: Who shared the 1923 Nobel Prize for the discovery of insulin?
questions.e: Banting shared his half with Charles Best.

questions.q: What is the most common primary malignant bone tumour in adolescents?
Roughly how many litres of blood does the heart pump per minute at rest?
questions.e: Cardiac output: heart rate × stroke volume.

questions.q: Which poison is classically said to smell of bitter almonds?
questions.e: Not everyone can smell it. It’s genetic.

questions.q: Which Persian physician wrote ‘The Canon of Medicine’ around 1025?
questions.e: Ibn Sina. A standard textbook for 600 years.

questions.q: What is the longest nerve in the human body?
Aspirin’s ancestor came from the bark of which tree?
Which creator of Sherlock Holmes was also a doctor?
questions.e: Holmes was based on his teacher, Dr Joseph Bell.

questions.q: What are the transverse grooves across the nails after a severe illness called?
What is the longest word in major English dictionaries, a lung disease from fine silica dust?
questions.e: Invented in 1935 to be the longest word. It worked.

questions.q: Who gave the first public demonstration of ether anaesthesia, in Boston in 1846?
questions.e: At Massachusetts General. The room is now the Ether Dome.

questions.q: What is the smallest skeletal muscle in the body?
questions.e: It dampens the stapes against loud noise.

questions.q: Drugs ending in ‘-pril’ belong to which class?
questions.e: Ramipril, perindopril and friends. Hello, dry cough.

questions.q: Kernig’s and Brudzinski’s signs are classic signs of what?
Which bacterium causes cat-scratch disease?
Who played paediatrician Doug Ross in ‘ER’?
‘Influenza’ comes from the Italian for what?
Which hormone does the pineal gland secrete?
Which physicist lived with motor neurone disease for over 50 years?
What is a borborygmus?
Who shared the 1962 Nobel Prize with Watson and Crick for DNA’s structure?
Reed–Sternberg cells are the hallmark of which cancer?
How many bones are in one human hand and wrist?
Which plant poison was used to execute Socrates?
Who pioneered antiseptic surgery using carbolic acid in the 1860s?
What are you actually hitting when you bang your ‘funny bone’?
What is the antidote to paracetamol overdose?
In ‘Scrubs’, who is JD’s reluctant mentor?
Which spots inside the mouth are an early sign of measles?
questions.e: Grains of salt on a red background.

questions.q: What is the medical term for brain freeze?
questions.e: From eating ice cream too fast.

questions.q: Who performed the first human-to-human heart transplant, in 1967?
questions.e: At Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town.

questions.q: Which organ contains the islets of Langerhans?
Sildenafil (Viagra) was first trialled for which condition?
questions.e: The side effect stole the show.

questions.q: Erb’s palsy is an injury to which nerve network?
Which virus causes both chickenpox and shingles?
Which city is the emergency department in ‘The Pitt’ set in?
‘Quarantine’ comes from the Italian for what?
questions.e: Quaranta giorni. Venice made plague ships wait.

questions.q: What is the normal pH range of arterial blood?
Which US president was paralysed by an illness diagnosed as polio in 1921?
What is the medical term for hiccups?
Which two scientists shared the 1945 Nobel Prize with Alexander Fleming?
questions.e: They turned penicillin into a usable drug.

questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes beriberi?
Roughly how many protein-coding genes are in the human genome?
Which metal caused the ‘mad hatter’ symptoms in hat makers?
Who was known as ‘the Lady with the Lamp’?
Which chamber of the heart has the thickest wall?
Which chemotherapy drug was first isolated from the Pacific yew tree?
Which 1966 film shrinks a medical team to travel through a man’s bloodstream?
Virchow’s triad describes the causes of what?
Which parts of the body have the highest density of sweat glands?
Who discovered X-rays in 1895?
questions.e: The first X-ray image was his wife’s hand.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.e: In the middle ear. About 3 mm.

questions.q: Semaglutide (Ozempic) mimics which gut hormone?
Whose sign is calf pain on dorsiflexion of the foot, once taught for DVT?
‘Typhoid Mary’ was a carrier of which bacterium?
What was Derek Shepherd’s nickname in ‘Grey’s Anatomy’?
‘Vaccine’ comes from the Latin for which animal?
Which ion mainly sets the resting membrane potential of cells?
Patient H.M. lost the ability to form new memories after surgery removed which structures?
What is the medical term for goosebumps?
Which two scientists won the 2005 Nobel Prize for showing H. pylori causes ulcers?
questions.e: Marshall drank a culture to prove it.

questions.q: The Philadelphia chromosome is a swap between which two chromosomes?
Roughly what is an average adult’s total lung capacity?
Which toxin, one of the most lethal known, is injected to smooth wrinkles?
In 1854, John Snow removed the handle of a cholera-spreading pump on which London street?
What is the largest internal organ?
Morphine is named after which Greek god?
What is the hospital called in ‘Scrubs’?
Cushing’s, Addison’s and Conn’s syndromes all involve which gland?
Which hormone was the first medicine made using recombinant DNA?
Which Paris obstetrician introduced incubators for premature babies in 1880, inspired by chicken incubators at the zoo?
questions.e: The poultry incubators were at the Jardin d’Acclimatation.

questions.q: Which fetal vessel joins the pulmonary artery to the aorta, and often stays open in premature babies?
questions.e: Its remnant is the ligamentum arteriosum.

questions.q: Which steroid did Liggins and Howie give mothers in their 1972 Auckland trial to mature preterm babies’ lungs?
questions.e: One of the great trials in obstetrics.

questions.q: The Ballard score estimates what in a newborn?
Which bacterium, carried harmlessly by many pregnant women, is a leading cause of early newborn sepsis?
Which BBC drama follows midwives and nuns in Poplar, in London’s East End, from the late 1950s?
‘Neonate’ comes from Greek and Latin roots meaning what?
Fetal haemoglobin has two alpha chains and two of which other chain?
questions.e: It grabs oxygen more tightly than adult haemoglobin.

questions.q: Which scientist, born prematurely on Christmas Day 1642, was said to be small enough to fit in a quart pot?
questions.e: His mother’s description. He lived to 84.

questions.q: What is the medical term for a baby’s first stool?
questions.e: From the Greek for poppy juice, after its dark colour.

questions.q: Who won the 2010 Nobel Prize for developing IVF?
questions.e: Louise Brown, the first IVF baby, was born in 1978.

questions.q: ‘Hyaline membrane disease’ is an old name for which condition of premature babies?
questions.e: Caused by a lack of surfactant. Accept RDS.

questions.q: Below what birth weight is a baby classed as low birth weight?
questions.e: Accept 2.5 kg. Under 1,500 g is very low birth weight.

questions.q: Which antibiotic caused ‘grey baby syndrome’ in newborns?
questions.e: Newborn livers can’t clear it fast enough.

questions.q: In 1922 Julius Hess opened the first US unit for premature babies in which city?
Which opening between the atria normally closes soon after birth?
questions.e: It stays open in about 1 in 4 adults.

questions.q: Which drug, also found in coffee, is used for apnoea of prematurity?
questions.e: As caffeine citrate. Some of the world’s smallest caffeine users.

questions.q: In ‘Friends’, who gives birth in ‘The One with the Birth’?
Which newborn reflex makes a baby fling out its arms when startled?
questions.e: Named after Austrian paediatrician Ernst Moro.

questions.q: Which Bogotá paediatrician introduced kangaroo mother care in 1978, when incubators were scarce?
questions.e: Parents became the incubator. Happy World Prematurity Day.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to qualify as a doctor in Britain, in 1865?
questions.e: Elizabeth Blackwell was registered earlier, with a US degree.

questions.q: Which flap of cartilage covers the windpipe when you swallow?
Drugs ending in ‘-olol’ belong to which class?
Which neurologist gave his name to the ‘march’ of a focal seizure?
Which disease does Mycobacterium leprae cause?
Which actor starred in both ‘ER’ and ‘The Pitt’?
questions.e: Dr John Carter, then Dr Robby.

questions.q: ‘Glaucoma’ comes from the Greek for which colour?
Which organ makes bile?
An iron rod passed through which lobe of Phineas Gage’s brain in 1848?
What is the anatomical name for the Adam’s apple?
Who won the 2015 Nobel Prize for discovering artemisinin for malaria?
questions.e: She found it in ancient Chinese texts.

questions.q: What is the most common cause of dementia?
What is the usual lower limit of a normal adult platelet count?
Which drug reverses a benzodiazepine overdose?
questions.e: Use with care. It can trigger seizures.

questions.q: Which pandemic killed perhaps a third of Europe in the 1340s?
What is the largest muscle in the body?
Which antibiotic, discovered in 1943, was the first effective treatment for tuberculosis?
questions.e: From soil bacteria. Nobel Prize in 1952.

questions.q: Who played the teenage title doctor in ‘Doogie Howser, M.D.’?
Murphy’s sign points to inflammation of which organ?
What is the fear of doctors called?
questions.e: Not to be confused with a reasonable fear of waiting rooms.
